name: Cutting the aśvattha with the weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga-śastra)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: The firmly rooted aśvattha — whose form, end, beginning and foundation are not perceived here — is to be cut with the strong weapon of non-attachment (asaṅga-śastra); then that place is to be sought from which those who reach it do not return, with the words 'I take refuge in that very primal person from whom the ancient stream of activity flowed forth' (15.3-15.4).
signs_of_progress: Those free from pride and delusion, who have conquered the fault of attachment, are constant in what pertains to the self, have turned from desires and are released from the pairs of pleasure and pain, go undeluded to that imperishable place (15.5).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Discerning the field and its knower (kṣetra-kṣetrajña)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Knowing the field (the body and its constituents, 13.2, 13.6-13.7) and its knower is called knowledge (13.3). Whoever knows puruṣa and prakṛti with the guṇas thus is not born again (13.24). The one who truly sees sees the supreme lord abiding equally in all beings (13.28), actions as done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer (13.30), and the separate existence of beings as resting in the one (13.31). Those who know the difference between field and knower with the eye of knowledge go to the highest (13.35).
signs_of_progress: Not born again (13.24); reaching brahman (13.31); going to the highest (13.35).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Reflecting on the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Keeping in view the evil of birth, death, old age, disease and pain is one of the items called knowledge (13.9; 13.8 in the 700-verse numbering).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Seeing that the guṇas act: non-doership
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Whoever sees actions done by prakṛti alone and oneself as not the doer sees truly (13.30); the seer who sees no doer other than the guṇas and knows what is beyond them attains the Lord's state (14.19); the one beyond the guṇas sits as one indifferent, unshaken, knowing 'it is the guṇas that act' (14.23).
signs_of_progress: Neither hating illumination, activity and delusion when present nor longing for them when gone (14.22).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Undivided devotion (ananya-bhakti)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Unswerving devotion to the Lord through a yoga with no other (ananya-yoga) is counted among the items called knowledge (13.11); whoever serves the Lord with unswerving bhakti-yoga goes beyond the guṇas and becomes fit for becoming brahman (14.26); knowing him as the highest person one worships him with one's whole being (15.19).

name: Resorting to solitude (vivikta-sthāna-sevana)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Resorting to secluded places (vivikta-deśa-sevitva) and finding no delight in the company of people are among the items called knowledge (13.11).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: After cutting the aśvattha with non-attachment, the place of no return is sought with the words 'I take refuge (prapadye) in that very primal person from whom the ancient stream of activity flowed forth' (15.4).

checks.note: Drawn by extractor B from the cited verses of ch. 13-15 only.

name: Cultivating sameness (samatva)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Constant evenness of thought amid the desired and the undesired is among the items called knowledge (13.10); the one beyond the guṇas is the same in pain and pleasure, toward clod, stone and gold, the pleasant and the unpleasant, blame and praise, honour and dishonour, friend and foe (14.24-14.25).

name: Dispassion (vairāgya)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Dispassion toward the objects of the senses is among the items called knowledge (13.9); non-attachment is the weapon that cuts the aśvattha (15.3).

name: Non-harming (ahiṃsā)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Non-harming is among the items called knowledge (13.8).

name: Service of the teacher
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Attendance on the teacher (ācāryopāsana) is among the items called knowledge (13.8).

name: Hearing the scriptures (śravaṇa)
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Those who do not know the self by meditation, sāṃkhya or the yoga of action worship having heard from others; holding to what they have heard, they too cross beyond death (13.26).

method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Some see the self in themselves by themselves through meditation (dhyāna) (13.25).

name: Karma-yoga: performing one's duty without attachment to the fruit
method_summary: Bhagavad Gītā 13–15: Some see the self through the yoga of action (karma-yoga) (13.25).
